types.name: ExecutionContextScope
types.summary: A child execution-context scope for nested dispatches: the handler opens a scope, passes ExecutionContextScope.Context to the inner mediator call, and disposes the scope when done. The child starts with clean items (isolation by default) and inherits the parent's cancellation token, so nested work stays on the outer cancellation chain. Disposing returns a pooled child to its pool — the context must not be used after the scope is disposed.
types.remarks: The scope is a struct: using var scope = ctx.CreateScope(); allocates nothing. An Abort() inside the child only aborts the inner pipeline; nothing ambient is overwritten, so there is no restore step — the parent context stays untouched in the caller's parameter.
types.syntax: public readonly struct ExecutionContextScope : IDisposable

types.name: GeneratedDispatchRoots
types.summary: Process-wide store of generically instantiated dispatch roots, populated by source-generated registration code. Each root closes a dispatch generic over a concrete message (and result) type at compile time, letting the dispatch caches construct their pipeline executors and invokers without [MakeGenericType(params Type[])](https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/api/system.type.makegenerictype) — and giving Native AOT and trimming a static anchor for every instantiation, value-type messages and results included, which shared generic code cannot cover. The reflective MakeGenericType paths remain as the fallback for types without a root (open generics, runtime-only registrations).
types.syntax: public static class GeneratedDispatchRoots

members.syntax: public static void AddResultPlan<TMessage, TResult, THandler>() where TMessage : notnull, IMessage where THandler : class, IAsyncHandler<TMessage, TResult>
members.summary: Result-producing counterpart of GeneratedDispatchRoots.AddVoidPlan<TMessage, THandler>(): roots a compile-time pipeline plan for a message whose entire pipeline is a single async result handler, so the dispatch executor invokes it devirtualized. The plan is advisory and re-validated per registry version exactly like the void plan. Idempotent.

members.name: AddResultPlan<TMessage, TResult, THandler>(Func<THandler>)
members.syntax: public static void AddResultPlan<TMessage, TResult, THandler>(Func<THandler> directHandlerFactory) where TMessage : notnull, IMessage where THandler : class, IAsyncHandler<TMessage, TResult>
members.summary: Variant of GeneratedDispatchRoots.AddResultPlan<TMessage, TResult, THandler>() carrying the compile-time handler construction path; see GeneratedDispatchRoots.AddVoidPlan<TMessage, THandler>(Func<THandler>) for the contract. Idempotent.

members.name: AddStream<TMessage, TResult>()
members.syntax: public static void AddStream<TMessage, TResult>() where TMessage : IMessage
members.summary: Roots the streaming dispatch generics of a message type. Idempotent.

members.name: AddVoidPlan<TMessage, THandler>()
members.syntax: public static void AddVoidPlan<TMessage, THandler>() where TMessage : notnull, IMessage where THandler : class, IAsyncHandler<TMessage>
members.summary: Roots a compile-time pipeline plan for a void message whose entire pipeline is a single async handler: the dispatch executor closes over both the message and the handler type, so the handler is invoked devirtualized — no contract pattern match. The plan is advisory: the executor re-validates the actual pipeline against the registry on every version change and falls back to the runtime dispatch shape whenever the pipeline no longer matches (interceptors registered at runtime, a different handler resolved, adapters configured). Idempotent.

members.name: AddVoidPlan<TMessage, THandler>(Func<THandler>)
members.syntax: public static void AddVoidPlan<TMessage, THandler>(Func<THandler> directHandlerFactory) where TMessage : notnull, IMessage where THandler : class, IAsyncHandler<TMessage>
members.summary: Variant of GeneratedDispatchRoots.AddVoidPlan<TMessage, THandler>() carrying a compile-time construction path for the handler: the generator emits static () => new THandler() for handlers with an accessible parameterless constructor that are not disposable. The factory is advisory like the plan itself — the executor uses it only after verifying at runtime that the handler's DI registration is the module's own plain transient one (no user factory, no lifetime override, not memoized), where container resolution and direct construction are semantically identical. Idempotent.

types.summary: A resolvable reference to a pipeline handler: the descriptor it was registered with, its pre-computed concrete type, and a way to obtain an instance for the current dispatch.

types.name: IResultAdapter
types.summary: Defines a contract for adapting and inspecting result objects of arbitrary types to extract exceptions without throwing them directly.
types.remarks: The primary purpose of a result adapter is to enable the framework to invoke exception interceptors based on exceptions contained within result objects, without having to throw these exceptions. This allows the message handling pipeline to process results and exceptions consistently, regardless of whether the exception occurred naturally or is wrapped inside a result type. Implementations of this interface allow the pipeline to remain agnostic to the specific result type returned by handlers, supporting result wrapper types such as FluentResult, OneOf, or any custom domain-specific result object. Multiple adapters can be registered in an IResultAdapterService, and each adapter is evaluated in order until one indicates it can adapt the result and successfully extracts an exception.

types.name: Discovery
types.summary: Runtime evaluation of the discovery attributes — the single source of truth for how ExcludeFromDiscoveryAttribute, DiscoveryKeyAttribute and key patterns compose. The reflection-based scanning paths (RegisterFromAssembly) call into this so their semantics stay identical to source-generated registration, which evaluates the same rules at compile time.
types.syntax: public static class Discovery

members.summary: Whether a single discovery key matches a pattern: ordinal equality, or — when the pattern ends with — an ordinal prefix match on the part before the star.

types.name: DiscoveryKeyAttribute
types.summary: Gates a registrable construct behind one or more discovery keys: a keyed type is excluded from default discovery (RegisterGenerated(), RegisterFromAssembly(assembly)) and registers only when a registration call selects one of its keys, e.g. RegisterGenerated("reporting") or RegisterGenerated("reporting.").
types.remarks: Untagged types carry the implicit default key (the empty string), which is what the pattern-less registration calls select. Listing the empty string alongside other keys ([DiscoveryKey("", "debug")]) keeps a type in default discovery while also making it selectable by key. Applied to an assembly, the attribute sets the default keys for every registrable type in that assembly that declares no DiscoveryKeyAttribute of its own — letting a library tag its whole surface (e.g. a modular-monolith module) in one place.
types.syntax:
[AttributeUsage(AttributeTargets.Assembly|AttributeTargets.Class|AttributeTargets.Struct|AttributeTargets.Interface, Inherited = false)]
public sealed class DiscoveryKeyAttribute : Attribute

members.name: DefaultKey
members.syntax: public const string DefaultKey = ""
members.summary: The default discovery key carried by types that declare no DiscoveryKeyAttribute: the empty string, selected by the pattern-less registration calls.

members.syntax: public DiscoveryKeyAttribute(params string[] keys)
members.summary: Gates a registrable construct behind one or more discovery keys: a keyed type is excluded from default discovery (RegisterGenerated(), RegisterFromAssembly(assembly)) and registers only when a registration call selects one of its keys, e.g. RegisterGenerated("reporting") or RegisterGenerated("reporting.").

members.summary: Gets the discovery keys assigned to the type or assembly.

types.name: ExcludeFromDiscoveryAttribute
types.summary: Excludes a registrable construct from automatic discovery entirely: both source-generated registration and reflection-based assembly scanning (RegisterFromAssembly) skip the type, regardless of discovery keys or patterns. Explicit registration (Register<T>(), Register(Type)) still works.
types.remarks: Applied to an assembly, the attribute removes every type in that assembly from discovery — for libraries that wire themselves up manually or are never meant to be scanned.
types.syntax:
[AttributeUsage(AttributeTargets.Assembly|AttributeTargets.Class|AttributeTargets.Struct|AttributeTargets.Interface, Inherited = false)]
public sealed class ExcludeFromDiscoveryAttribute : Attribute

types.name: ExcludeFromPipelineAttribute
types.summary: Excludes a message from covariantly matched interceptors: interceptors registered against a base type or interface of the message (e.g. an IEvent-wide pre-interceptor) no longer apply to it. Interceptors registered against the message type itself always run — they were written for this message deliberately.
types.remarks: Without arguments every covariantly matched interceptor is excluded; with group names only the covariant interceptors carrying one of those GroupAttribute groups are. Main handlers are never affected — the attribute shapes the interceptor pipeline, not dispatch itself.
types.syntax:
[AttributeUsage(AttributeTargets.Class|AttributeTargets.Struct|AttributeTargets.Interface, Inherited = false)]
public sealed class ExcludeFromPipelineAttribute : Attribute

types.name: ICommand
types.summary: Base command and a marker interface that can be registered by command module
types.syntax: public interface ICommand : IMessage

types.name: ICommand<TResult>
types.summary: Represents a command that produces a result of type TResult when handled.
types.remarks: This interface extends the base ICommand interface to support commands that need to return data to the caller. While regular commands are used for state-changing operations without returning data, commands with results allow for obtaining computed values or status information from the handler.
types.syntax: public interface ICommand<TResult> : ICommand, IMessage

typeParameters.name: TResult
typeParameters.description: The type of result that will be returned when the command is processed.

types.name: ICommandExceptionInterceptor
types.summary: Represents a non-type-safe exception interceptor for commands.
types.remarks: This interceptor can handle any ICommand without specifying a particular result type. It returns object from the HandleAsync method, making it suitable for scenarios where you want to apply exception handling logic across multiple command types in a generic pipeline without caring about the exact result type. For scenarios where type safety is required, use the generic version: ICommandExceptionInterceptor<TCommand, TResult>.
types.syntax: public interface ICommandExceptionInterceptor : ICommand, IMessage, IAsyncExceptionInterceptor<ICommand>, IExceptionInterceptor

types.name: ICommandExceptionInterceptor<TCommand, TResult>
types.summary: Represents a type-safe exception interceptor for commands with a strongly-typed result. The interceptor can inspect the exception and modify or replace the command result.
types.remarks: TCommand is contravariant, matching the core IAsyncExceptionInterceptor<TMessage, TResult> contract the typed dispatch matches against. TResult must stay invariant: the typed member returns it.
types.syntax: public interface ICommandExceptionInterceptor<in TCommand, TResult> : ICommand, IMessage, IAsyncExceptionInterceptor<TCommand, TResult>, IExceptionInterceptor where TCommand : ICommand<TResult> where TResult : notnull

typeParameters.name: TCommand
typeParameters.description: The command type being intercepted. Must implement ICommand<TResult>.

typeParameters.name: TResult
typeParameters.description: The result type of the command. Also, the type returned by the interceptor — for a narrower return type there is no third parameter anymore; return the base result type.

members.name: HandleAsync(TCommand, TResult?, Exception, IExecutionContext)
members.syntax: ValueTask<TResult?> HandleAsync(TCommand command, TResult? result, Exception exception, IExecutionContext context)
members.summary: Handles the exception asynchronously, potentially modifying the command result.
members.returns: ValueTask<TResult> — A ValueTask<TResult> producing the (possibly modified) result that continues through the pipeline.

parameters.name: command
parameters.description: The command being processed when the exception occurred.

parameters.name: result
parameters.description: The result produced before the exception occurred, if any.

parameters.name: exception
parameters.description: The exception thrown during pipeline execution.

parameters.name: context
parameters.description: The current execution context.

types.name: ICommandExceptionInterceptor<TCommand>
types.summary: Marker interface for asynchronous exception interceptors for commands. Inherits IAsyncExceptionInterceptor<TMessage, TResult> and ICommand to allow registration within the command module. This interface does not modify the behavior or return type; interception logic is handled by IAsyncExceptionInterceptor<TMessage, TResult>.
types.remarks: ICommandExceptionInterceptor<in TCommand, in ValueTask, ValueTask> or other type-safe variants, which preserve the exact result type.
types.syntax: public interface ICommandExceptionInterceptor<in TCommand> : ICommand, IMessage, IAsyncExceptionInterceptor<TCommand, object>, IExceptionInterceptor where TCommand : ICommand

typeParameters.name: TCommand
typeParameters.description: The type of command being intercepted. Must implement ICommand

types.name: ICommandFinalInterceptor
types.summary: Represents a final interceptor for commands that can be registered without specifying a particular command type.
types.remarks: This is a non-type-safe version of a command final interceptor. It allows intercepting the final stage of any command pipeline regardless of the concrete command type. Use this interface when you want to apply final logic (e.g., logging, cleanup) across multiple command types without requiring a strongly typed command. For scenarios requiring type safety, prefer using the generic version: ICommandFinalInterceptor<TCommand> or ICommandFinalInterceptor<TCommand, TResult>.
types.syntax: public interface ICommandFinalInterceptor : ICommand, IMessage, IAsyncFinalInterceptor<ICommand>, IFinalInterceptor

types.name: ICommandFinalInterceptor<TCommand, TResult>
types.summary: Represents a final interceptor for commands in the pipeline with a strongly typed result.
types.remarks: A final interceptor is executed at the end of the pipeline, after pre-, post-, and exception interceptors. It can observe the command, its result, or any exception thrown, but it should not directly modify the result. Use this interface to perform logging, cleanup, or any last-step operations while preserving the type safety of the command's result.
types.syntax: public interface ICommandFinalInterceptor<in TCommand, in TResult> : ICommand, IMessage, IAsyncFinalInterceptor<TCommand, TResult>, IFinalInterceptor where TCommand : ICommand<in TResult>

typeParameters.name: TCommand
typeParameters.description: The type of command this interceptor handles. Must implement ICommand<TResult>.

typeParameters.name: TResult
typeParameters.description: The type of the result produced by the command.

types.name: ICommandFinalInterceptor<TCommand>
types.summary: Represents a final interceptor for commands in the pipeline.
types.remarks: A final interceptor is always executed at the end of the pipeline, after pre-, post-, and exception interceptors. It can observe the message, result, or exception, but should not modify the result directly. Use this interface to perform logging, cleanup, or any last-step operations in the command pipeline.
types.syntax: public interface ICommandFinalInterceptor<in TCommand> : ICommand, IMessage, IAsyncFinalInterceptor<TCommand>, IFinalInterceptor where TCommand : ICommand

typeParameters.name: TCommand
typeParameters.description: The type of command this interceptor handles. Must implement ICommand.

types.name: ICommandHandler<TCommand, TResult>
types.summary: Represents a handler for commands that produce a strongly-typed result.
types.remarks: Use this interface when you want type-safe handling of commands with a specific result type. The handler processes the command asynchronously and returns the strongly-typed result.
types.syntax: public interface ICommandHandler<in TCommand, TResult> : ICommand, IMessage, IAsyncHandler<TCommand, TResult>, IHandler where TCommand : ICommand<TResult>

typeParameters.name: TCommand
typeParameters.description: The type of command this handler processes. Must implement ICommand<TResult>.

typeParameters.name: TResult
typeParameters.description: The type of result produced by the command.

types.name: ICommandHandler<TCommand>
types.summary: Represents a handler for commands implementing ICommand.
types.remarks: This interface is non-generic regarding the result type; the command may or may not produce a result. For commands with a strongly typed result, consider using ICommandHandler<TCommand, TResult>.
types.syntax: public interface ICommandHandler<in TCommand> : ICommand, IMessage, IAsyncHandler<TCommand>, IHandler where TCommand : ICommand

typeParameters.name: TCommand
typeParameters.description: The type of command this handler processes. Must implement ICommand.

types.name: ICommandMediator
types.summary: Represents the mediator interface for sending commands within the application.
types.remarks: The command mediator is responsible for routing commands to their appropriate handlers and orchestrating the command handling pipeline. It ensures that commands are processed by exactly one handler and provides methods for sending commands both with and without expected results. In the CQRS pattern, commands represent intentions to change the system state. The command mediator helps maintain separation between the command issuers and the command handlers.
types.syntax: public interface ICommandMediator

types.name: ICommandPostInterceptor
types.summary: Represents a post-processing interceptor for commands that executes after any ICommand is handled.
types.remarks: This interceptor is non-generic and non-type-safe. It can be registered to run for multiple command types without specifying a particular result type. The HandleAsync method returns object, so any result modifications are handled via object references and casting. For scenarios where type safety is required, use the generic version: ICommandPostInterceptor<TCommand, TResult>.
types.syntax: public interface ICommandPostInterceptor : ICommand, IMessage, IAsyncPostInterceptor<ICommand>, IPostInterceptor

types.name: ICommandPostInterceptor<TCommand, TResult>
types.summary: Represents a type-safe post-interceptor for commands with a strongly-typed result. Executes after the command handler has completed and can modify the result before it propagates further through the pipeline.
types.remarks: TCommand is contravariant, matching the core IAsyncPostInterceptor<TMessage, TResult> contract the typed dispatch matches against. TResult must stay invariant: the typed member returns it.
types.syntax: public interface ICommandPostInterceptor<in TCommand, TResult> : ICommand, IMessage, IAsyncPostInterceptor<TCommand, TResult>, IPostInterceptor where TCommand : ICommand<TResult> where TResult : notnull

typeParameters.name: TCommand
typeParameters.description: The command type being intercepted. Must implement ICommand<TResult>.

typeParameters.name: TResult
typeParameters.description: The result type of the command. Also the type returned by the interceptor — for a narrower return type there is no third parameter anymore; return the base result type.

members.name: HandleAsync(TCommand, TResult, IExecutionContext)
members.syntax: ValueTask<TResult> HandleAsync(TCommand command, TResult commandResult, IExecutionContext context)
members.summary: Handles the post-processing of a command asynchronously.

parameters.description: The command that was executed.

parameters.name: commandResult
parameters.description: The result produced by the command handler.

parameters.name: context
parameters.description: The current execution context.

types.name: ICommandPostInterceptor<TCommand>
types.summary: Represents a post-processing interceptor for commands. This non-generic, non-type-safe version returns object from the pipeline.
types.remarks: Use this interface to register post-interceptors in the command pipeline without specifying a strongly-typed result. For type-safe scenarios, prefer using the generic version: ICommandPostInterceptor<TCommand, TResult>.
types.syntax: public interface ICommandPostInterceptor<in TCommand> : ICommand, IMessage, IAsyncPostInterceptor<TCommand>, IPostInterceptor where TCommand : ICommand

typeParameters.name: TCommand
typeParameters.description: The type of command this interceptor handles. Must implement ICommand.

types.name: ICommandPreInterceptor
types.summary: Represents a pre-interceptor for commands that is invoked before the command enters the pipeline. Can be used to modify the command or perform preparatory actions.
types.remarks: This is a non-generic, non-type-safe version of a pre-interceptor. It works with any command implementing ICommand. For type-safe interception, consider using ICommandPreInterceptor<TCommand> or ICommandPreInterceptor<TCommand, TModifiedCommand>.
types.syntax: public interface ICommandPreInterceptor : ICommand, IMessage, IAsyncPreInterceptor<ICommand>, IPreInterceptor

types.name: ICommandPreInterceptor<TCommand, TModifiedCommand>
types.summary: Represents a type-safe pre-interceptor for commands, allowing modification of the command before it enters the pipeline.
types.remarks: This interface is the type-safe variant of ICommandPreInterceptor. Use this when you want to ensure compile-time type safety while allowing the command to be modified before entering the pipeline. The HandleAsync method is called before the command is processed. The returned TModifiedCommand will continue through the pipeline as the new command.
types.syntax: public interface ICommandPreInterceptor<in TCommand, TModifiedCommand> : ICommand, IMessage, IAsyncPreInterceptor<TCommand>, IPreInterceptor where TCommand : ICommand where TModifiedCommand : TCommand

typeParameters.name: TCommand
typeParameters.description: The type of command being intercepted. Must implement ICommand.

typeParameters.name: TModifiedCommand
typeParameters.description: The type of the command returned after interception. Must be assignable from TCommand. This allows modifying or replacing the original command in a type-safe way.

types.name: ICommandPreInterceptor<TCommand>
types.summary: Defines a type-safe pre-interceptor for a command. It runs before the handler and returns the command that continues through the pipeline — the original instance, or a rewritten one.
types.remarks: A pre-interceptor carries no result, so — unlike the post/exception interceptors, whose second type parameter is the result — the single-parameter form returns the command type directly rather than object. Use the non-generic ICommandPreInterceptor to intercept any command (returning object), or ICommandPreInterceptor<TCommand, TModifiedCommand> to return a different, derived command type. TCommand is invariant because it is returned.
types.syntax: public interface ICommandPreInterceptor<TCommand> : ICommand, IMessage, IAsyncPreInterceptor<TCommand>, IPreInterceptor where TCommand : ICommand

typeParameters.name: TCommand
typeParameters.description: The type of command to intercept.

types.name: IQuery
types.summary: Represents a query message in the system, which can be dispatched through the query module.
types.remarks: Any type implementing IQuery is considered a query and can be registered within the query module, allowing it to be handled by query handlers and interceptors. Queries are typically read-only operations that return a result, and they participate in the query mediation pipeline.
types.syntax: public interface IQuery : IMessage

types.name: IQuery<TResult>
types.summary: Represents a type-safe query message that produces a result of type TResult.
types.remarks: This interface extends IQuery and is intended for queries that return a specific result type when handled by a query handler. Implementing IQuery<TResult> allows the query to be registered within the query module and processed by type-safe query handlers and interceptors.
types.syntax: public interface IQuery<TResult> : IQuery, IMessage

typeParameters.name: TResult
typeParameters.description: The type of result returned by the query.

types.name: IQueryExceptionInterceptor
types.summary: Represents a query exception interceptor that can handle multiple query types in a non-generic, non-type-safe manner.
types.remarks: This interceptor is useful when you want a single exception interceptor to run for multiple query types without defining separate generic implementations. Implementations will receive queries as IQuery and results as object. For scenarios requiring type-safe handling of a specific query type and result type, consider using IQueryExceptionInterceptor<TQuery, TResult> instead.
types.syntax: public interface IQueryExceptionInterceptor : IQuery, IMessage, IAsyncExceptionInterceptor<IQuery>, IExceptionInterceptor

types.name: IQueryExceptionInterceptor<TQuery, TResult>
types.summary: Represents a type-safe exception interceptor for queries with a strongly-typed result. The interceptor can inspect the exception and modify or replace the query result.
types.remarks: TQuery is contravariant, matching the core IAsyncExceptionInterceptor<TMessage, TResult> contract the typed dispatch matches against. TResult must stay invariant: the typed member returns it.
types.syntax: public interface IQueryExceptionInterceptor<in TQuery, TResult> : IQuery, IMessage, IAsyncExceptionInterceptor<TQuery, TResult>, IExceptionInterceptor where TQuery : IQuery<TResult> where TResult : notnull

typeParameters.name: TQuery

types.name: IEvent
types.summary: Represents a message or handler that is recognized by the event module.
types.remarks: Any message type that implements IEvent is automatically treated as an event by the messaging infrastructure. Similarly, event handlers must implement or be decorated with IEvent to be registered within the event module. The event module also supports simple POCO objects (plain old CLR objects), allowing them to be registered and used as events. Events are typically used in pub/sub scenarios, broadcasting information to multiple handlers without expecting a return value. Implementing IEvent indicates that a message or handler is registrable and discoverable within the event module for event dispatching.
types.syntax: public interface IEvent : IMessage

types.remarks: This interface is a non-generic version of IEventExceptionInterceptor<TEvent>, applying to all events implementing IEvent. It inherits from IAsyncExceptionInterceptor<TMessage, TResult>, enabling asynchronous exception handling after event handlers have been invoked. Event handlers and messages that implement IEvent will recognize this interceptor automatically in the event mediation pipeline.

types.summary: Represents an asynchronous exception interceptor for events, allowing custom logic to execute when an exception occurs during event handling.
types.remarks: Implementing this interface allows the interceptor to participate in the event mediation pipeline when an exception is thrown during the handling of TEvent. This interface inherits from IAsyncExceptionInterceptor<TMessage>, enabling asynchronous exception handling logic. The TEvent type must be non-nullable and implement IEvent.

types.summary: Represents a non-generic final interceptor for events, allowing custom logic to execute after all event handlers and other interceptors have completed.
types.remarks: This interface is a non-generic version of IEventFinalInterceptor<TEvent>, applying to all events implementing IEvent. It inherits from IAsyncFinalInterceptor<TMessage>, enabling asynchronous final processing of events after they are dispatched to their handlers. Event handlers and messages that implement IEvent will recognize this interceptor automatically in the event mediation pipeline.

types.remarks: Implementing IEventFinalInterceptor<TEvent> allows the interceptor to participate in the event mediation pipeline at the final stage, after all handlers and other interceptors have run. This interface inherits from IAsyncFinalInterceptor<TMessage, TResult>, so final-interceptor logic can be asynchronous and return a ValueTask. The TEvent type must implement IEvent.

Handlers should implement the IAsyncHandler<TMessage> interface to provide asynchronous processing logic for the event.

types.name: IEventMediator
types.summary: Represents the mediator interface for publishing events within the application.
types.remarks: The event mediator is responsible for broadcasting events to all registered handlers and orchestrating the event handling pipeline. Unlike commands, which are handled by exactly one handler, events can be handled by multiple handlers, allowing for decoupled communication between different parts of the application. In the publish-subscribe pattern, events represent notifications about something that has happened in the system. The event mediator helps maintain separation between the event publishers and the event subscribers (handlers).

types.remarks: This interface is a non-generic version of IEventPreInterceptor<TEvent>, applying to all events implementing IEvent. It inherits from IAsyncPreInterceptor<TMessage>, enabling asynchronous pre-processing of events before they are dispatched to their handlers. Event handlers and messages that implement IEvent will recognize this interceptor automatically in the event mediation pipeline.

This interface inherits from IAsyncPreInterceptor<TMessage>, enabling asynchronous pre-processing in the event mediation pipeline.

types.name: IEventPreInterceptor<TEvent>
types.summary: Represents a type-safe pre-interceptor for events. It runs before the event handlers and returns the event that continues through the pipeline — the original, or a rewritten one.
types.remarks: A pre-interceptor carries no result, so the single-parameter form returns the event type directly rather than object. Use the non-generic IEventPreInterceptor to intercept any event, or IEventPreInterceptor<TEvent, TModifiedEvent> to return a different, derived event type. TEvent is invariant because it is returned.

types.name: IPublisher
types.summary: Represents the mediator interface for publishing events within the application.
types.remarks: The event mediator is responsible for broadcasting events to all registered handlers and orchestrating the event handling pipeline. Unlike commands, which are handled by exactly one handler, events can be handled by multiple handlers, allowing for decoupled communication between different parts of the application. In the publish-subscribe pattern, events represent notifications about something that has happened in the system. The event mediator helps maintain separation between the event publishers and the event subscribers (handlers).
types.syntax: public interface IPublisher : IEventMediator

types.name: MessageDispatchEngine
types.summary: The scope-free dispatch engine behind every mediator facade: the pipeline-executor lookup, pooled execution context, and completion handling of the IMessageMediator executor path, with the calling scope's provider supplied per call instead of being captured per instance. One process-wide singleton serves every scope, so resolving an engine-backed facade builds exactly one object per resolution.
types.remarks: Construction is internal: the engine only makes sense wired to the process-wide PipelineExecutorCache and dependencies factory that the DI registration supplies. Dispatch behavior matches IMessageMediator's executor overloads exactly — the mediator delegates here, passing its own captured provider.

types.name: ResultAdapterService
types.summary: Implementation of IResultAdapterService that manages a collection of IResultAdapter instances and provides exception lookup functionality.
types.remarks: This service allows the pipeline to remain agnostic of the result type while still extracting exceptions when necessary. Multiple adapters can be registered to handle different result styles (e.g., plain values, FluentResults, OneOf types, or custom wrappers). The adapters are evaluated in the order they were added, and the first adapter capable of adapting the result will be used to extract an exception.

types.name: ExecutionContextScope
types.summary: A child execution-context scope for nested dispatches: the handler opens a scope, passes ExecutionContextScope.Context to the inner mediator call, and disposes the scope when done. The child starts with clean items (isolation by default) and inherits the parent's cancellation token, so nested work stays on the outer cancellation chain. Disposing returns a pooled child to its pool — the context must not be used after the scope is disposed.
types.remarks: The scope is a struct: using var scope = ctx.CreateScope(); allocates nothing. An Abort() inside the child only aborts the inner pipeline; nothing ambient is overwritten, so there is no restore step — the parent context stays untouched in the caller's parameter.
types.syntax: public readonly struct ExecutionContextScope : IDisposable

types.summary: Process-wide lookup of compile-time-computed handler descriptors, populated by source-generated module initializers: one factory per handler type the generator saw in a compilation. Runtime registration (Register<THandler>() / Register(Type)) consults the catalog first and only falls back to the reflection-based descriptor builders for types no generator modeled — runtime-loaded plugin types, open generics registered manually, foreign assemblies without the analyzer. The generator's descriptor computation mirrors the runtime builders exactly (the contract its test suite pins), so the two paths are interchangeable; the catalog only removes the reflection.

types.name: GeneratedDispatchRoots
types.summary: Process-wide store of generically instantiated dispatch roots, populated by source-generated registration code. Each root closes a dispatch generic over a concrete message (and result) type at compile time, letting the dispatch caches construct their pipeline executors and invokers without [MakeGenericType(params Type[])](https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/api/system.type.makegenerictype) — and giving Native AOT and trimming a static anchor for every instantiation, value-type messages and results included, which shared generic code cannot cover. The reflective MakeGenericType paths remain as the fallback for types without a root (open generics, runtime-only registrations).
types.syntax: public static class GeneratedDispatchRoots

members.summary: Result-producing counterpart of GeneratedDispatchRoots.AddVoidPlan<TMessage, THandler>(): roots a compile-time pipeline plan for a message whose entire pipeline is a single async result handler, so the dispatch executor invokes it devirtualized. The plan is advisory and re-validated per registry version exactly like the void plan. Idempotent.

members.syntax: public static void AddResultPlan<TMessage, TResult, THandler>(Func<THandler> directHandlerFactory) where TMessage : notnull, IMessage where THandler : class, IAsyncHandler<TMessage, TResult>
members.summary: Variant of GeneratedDispatchRoots.AddResultPlan<TMessage, TResult, THandler>() carrying the compile-time handler construction path; see GeneratedDispatchRoots.AddVoidPlan<TMessage, THandler>(Func<THandler>) for the contract. Idempotent.

members.syntax: public static void AddStream<TMessage, TResult>() where TMessage : IMessage
members.summary: Roots the streaming dispatch generics of a message type. Idempotent.

members.name: AddVoidPlan<TMessage, THandler>()
members.syntax: public static void AddVoidPlan<TMessage, THandler>() where TMessage : notnull, IMessage where THandler : class, IAsyncHandler<TMessage>
members.summary: Roots a compile-time pipeline plan for a void message whose entire pipeline is a single async handler: the dispatch executor closes over both the message and the handler type, so the handler is invoked devirtualized — no contract pattern match. The plan is advisory: the executor re-validates the actual pipeline against the registry on every version change and falls back to the runtime dispatch shape whenever the pipeline no longer matches (interceptors registered at runtime, a different handler resolved, adapters configured). Idempotent.

members.name: AddVoidPlan<TMessage, THandler>(Func<THandler>)
members.syntax: public static void AddVoidPlan<TMessage, THandler>(Func<THandler> directHandlerFactory) where TMessage : notnull, IMessage where THandler : class, IAsyncHandler<TMessage>
members.summary: Variant of GeneratedDispatchRoots.AddVoidPlan<TMessage, THandler>() carrying a compile-time construction path for the handler: the generator emits static () => new THandler() for handlers with an accessible parameterless constructor that are not disposable. The factory is advisory like the plan itself — the executor uses it only after verifying at runtime that the handler's DI registration is the module's own plain transient one (no user factory, no lifetime override, not memoized), where container resolution and direct construction are semantically identical. Idempotent.

types.name: GroupSet
types.summary: An immutable, canonicalized group filter: [GroupSet.Of(params string[])](/ergosfare.docs/preview/api/core-abstractions/groupset#ofparams-string) interns equal sequences (same names, same order — ordinal) to one instance, so the grouped dispatch caches can match a reused filter with a single reference check instead of comparing group names element-wise. Define filters once and reuse them: A GroupSet is also an IReadOnlyList<T> of its names, so it can be assigned anywhere a group sequence is accepted (settings.Filters.Groups = Reporting;) — the caches recognize it there too.
types.remarks: Interning is bounded: beyond an internal cap, [GroupSet.Of(params string[])](/ergosfare.docs/preview/api/core-abstractions/groupset#ofparams-string) returns un-interned instances, which still dispatch correctly — the caches fall back to comparing group names. Group names come from code in practice, so the cap exists only as a guard against pathological dynamic name generation.

types.name: IResultAdapter
types.summary: Defines a contract for adapting and inspecting result objects of arbitrary types to extract exceptions without throwing them directly.
types.remarks: The primary purpose of a result adapter is to enable the framework to invoke exception interceptors based on exceptions contained within result objects, without having to throw these exceptions. This allows the message handling pipeline to process results and exceptions consistently, regardless of whether the exception occurred naturally or is wrapped inside a result type. Implementations of this interface allow the pipeline to remain agnostic to the specific result type returned by handlers, supporting result wrapper types such as FluentResult, OneOf, or any custom domain-specific result object. Multiple adapters can be registered in an IResultAdapterService, and each adapter is evaluated in order until one indicates it can adapt the result and successfully extracts an exception.

types.name: Discovery
types.summary: Runtime evaluation of the discovery attributes — the single source of truth for how ExcludeFromDiscoveryAttribute, DiscoveryKeyAttribute and key patterns compose. The reflection-based scanning paths (RegisterFromAssembly) call into this so their semantics stay identical to source-generated registration, which evaluates the same rules at compile time.
types.syntax: public static class Discovery

members.syntax: public static string[] GetKeys(Type type)

members.syntax: public static bool Matches(Type type, string discoveryKeyPattern)
members.summary: Whether discovery with the given key pattern selects the type: the type is not excluded from discovery, and at least one of its effective discovery keys matches the pattern.

parameters.name: type
parameters.description: The candidate registrable type.

parameters.description: The key pattern: an exact key, a prefix glob with a trailing (e.g. "reporting."), or the empty string for default discovery.

members.syntax: public static bool MatchesKey(string key, string discoveryKeyPattern)
members.summary: Whether a single discovery key matches a pattern: ordinal equality, or — when the pattern ends with — an ordinal prefix match on the part before the star.

types.name: DiscoveryKeyAttribute
types.summary: Gates a registrable construct behind one or more discovery keys: a keyed type is excluded from default discovery (RegisterGenerated(), RegisterFromAssembly(assembly)) and registers only when a registration call selects one of its keys, e.g. RegisterGenerated("reporting") or RegisterGenerated("reporting.").
types.remarks: Untagged types carry the implicit default key (the empty string), which is what the pattern-less registration calls select. Listing the empty string alongside other keys ([DiscoveryKey("", "debug")]) keeps a type in default discovery while also making it selectable by key. Applied to an assembly, the attribute sets the default keys for every registrable type in that assembly that declares no DiscoveryKeyAttribute of its own — letting a library tag its whole surface (e.g. a modular-monolith module) in one place.
types.syntax:
[AttributeUsage(AttributeTargets.Assembly|AttributeTargets.Class|AttributeTargets.Struct|AttributeTargets.Interface, Inherited = false)]
public sealed class DiscoveryKeyAttribute : Attribute

members.name: DefaultKey
members.syntax: public const string DefaultKey = ""
members.summary: The default discovery key carried by types that declare no DiscoveryKeyAttribute: the empty string, selected by the pattern-less registration calls.

members.name: DiscoveryKeyAttribute(params string[])
members.syntax: public DiscoveryKeyAttribute(params string[] keys)
members.summary: Gates a registrable construct behind one or more discovery keys: a keyed type is excluded from default discovery (RegisterGenerated(), RegisterFromAssembly(assembly)) and registers only when a registration call selects one of its keys, e.g. RegisterGenerated("reporting") or RegisterGenerated("reporting.").

members.name: Keys
members.syntax: public string[] Keys { get; }
members.summary: Gets the discovery keys assigned to the type or assembly.

types.name: ExcludeFromDiscoveryAttribute
types.summary: Excludes a registrable construct from automatic discovery entirely: both source-generated registration and reflection-based assembly scanning (RegisterFromAssembly) skip the type, regardless of discovery keys or patterns. Explicit registration (Register<T>(), Register(Type)) still works.
types.remarks: Applied to an assembly, the attribute removes every type in that assembly from discovery — for libraries that wire themselves up manually or are never meant to be scanned.
types.syntax:
[AttributeUsage(AttributeTargets.Assembly|AttributeTargets.Class|AttributeTargets.Struct|AttributeTargets.Interface, Inherited = false)]
public sealed class ExcludeFromDiscoveryAttribute : Attribute

types.name: ExcludeFromPipelineAttribute
types.summary: Excludes a message from covariantly matched interceptors: interceptors registered against a base type or interface of the message (e.g. an IEvent-wide pre-interceptor) no longer apply to it. Interceptors registered against the message type itself always run — they were written for this message deliberately.
types.remarks: Without arguments every covariantly matched interceptor is excluded; with group names only the covariant interceptors carrying one of those GroupAttribute groups are. Main handlers are never affected — the attribute shapes the interceptor pipeline, not dispatch itself.
types.syntax:
[AttributeUsage(AttributeTargets.Class|AttributeTargets.Struct|AttributeTargets.Interface, Inherited = false)]
public sealed class ExcludeFromPipelineAttribute : Attribute

members.syntax: public ExcludeFromPipelineAttribute(params string[] groups)

Interceptors registered against the message type itself always run — they were written for this message deliberately.

types.name: ICommand
types.summary: Base command and a marker interface that can be registered by command module
types.syntax: public interface ICommand : IMessage

types.name: ICommand<TResult>
types.summary: Represents a command that produces a result of type TResult when handled.
types.remarks: This interface extends the base ICommand interface to support commands that need to return data to the caller. While regular commands are used for state-changing operations without returning data, commands with results allow for obtaining computed values or status information from the handler.
types.syntax: public interface ICommand<TResult> : ICommand, IMessage

typeParameters.name: TResult
typeParameters.description: The type of result that will be returned when the command is processed.

types.name: ICommandExceptionInterceptor
types.summary: Represents a non-type-safe exception interceptor for commands.
types.remarks: This interceptor can handle any ICommand without specifying a particular result type. It returns object from the HandleAsync method, making it suitable for scenarios where you want to apply exception handling logic across multiple command types in a generic pipeline without caring about the exact result type. For scenarios where type safety is required, use the generic version: ICommandExceptionInterceptor<TCommand, TResult>.
types.syntax: public interface ICommandExceptionInterceptor : ICommand, IMessage, IAsyncExceptionInterceptor<ICommand>, IExceptionInterceptor

types.name: ICommandExceptionInterceptor<TCommand, TResult>
types.summary: Represents a type-safe exception interceptor for commands with a strongly-typed result. The interceptor can inspect the exception and modify or replace the command result.
types.remarks: TCommand is contravariant, matching the core IAsyncExceptionInterceptor<TMessage, TResult> contract the typed dispatch matches against. TResult must stay invariant: the typed member returns it.
types.syntax: public interface ICommandExceptionInterceptor<in TCommand, TResult> : ICommand, IMessage, IAsyncExceptionInterceptor<TCommand, TResult>, IExceptionInterceptor where TCommand : ICommand<TResult> where TResult : notnull

typeParameters.name: TCommand
typeParameters.description: The command type being intercepted. Must implement ICommand<TResult>.

typeParameters.name: TResult
typeParameters.description: The result type of the command. Also, the type returned by the interceptor — for a narrower return type there is no third parameter anymore; return the base result type.

members.name: HandleAsync(TCommand, TResult?, Exception, IExecutionContext)
members.syntax: ValueTask<TResult?> HandleAsync(TCommand command, TResult? result, Exception exception, IExecutionContext context)
members.summary: Handles the exception asynchronously, potentially modifying the command result.
members.returns: ValueTask<TResult> — A ValueTask<TResult> producing the (possibly modified) result that continues through the pipeline.

parameters.name: command
parameters.description: The command being processed when the exception occurred.

parameters.name: result
parameters.description: The result produced before the exception occurred, if any.

parameters.name: exception
parameters.description: The exception thrown during pipeline execution.

parameters.name: context
parameters.description: The current execution context.

types.name: ICommandExceptionInterceptor<TCommand>
types.summary: Marker interface for asynchronous exception interceptors for commands. Inherits the result-agnostic IAsyncExceptionInterceptor<TMessage> and ICommand to allow registration within the command module. This interface does not modify the behavior or return type; interception logic is handled by IAsyncExceptionInterceptor<TMessage>.
types.remarks: The result-agnostic base is deliberate: a result-typed base (the previous IAsyncExceptionInterceptor<TCommand, object>) is invisible to the pipeline's pattern match whenever the pipeline result is a value type — void command pipelines carry a ValueTask result internally, so the exception stage failed with NotSupportedException the moment it ran. For a strongly-typed result use ICommandExceptionInterceptor<TCommand, TResult>.
types.syntax: public interface ICommandExceptionInterceptor<in TCommand> : ICommand, IMessage, IAsyncExceptionInterceptor<TCommand>, IExceptionInterceptor where TCommand : ICommand

typeParameters.name: TCommand
typeParameters.description: The type of command being intercepted. Must implement ICommand

types.name: ICommandFinalInterceptor
types.summary: Represents a final interceptor for commands that can be registered without specifying a particular command type.
types.remarks: This is a non-type-safe version of a command final interceptor. It allows intercepting the final stage of any command pipeline regardless of the concrete command type. Use this interface when you want to apply final logic (e.g., logging, cleanup) across multiple command types without requiring a strongly typed command. For scenarios requiring type safety, prefer using the generic version: ICommandFinalInterceptor<TCommand> or ICommandFinalInterceptor<TCommand, TResult>.
types.syntax: public interface ICommandFinalInterceptor : ICommand, IMessage, IAsyncFinalInterceptor<ICommand>, IFinalInterceptor

types.name: ICommandFinalInterceptor<TCommand, TResult>
types.summary: Represents a final interceptor for commands in the pipeline with a strongly typed result.
types.remarks: A final interceptor is executed at the end of the pipeline, after pre-, post-, and exception interceptors. It can observe the command, its result, or any exception thrown, but it should not directly modify the result. Use this interface to perform logging, cleanup, or any last-step operations while preserving the type safety of the command's result.
types.syntax: public interface ICommandFinalInterceptor<in TCommand, in TResult> : ICommand, IMessage, IAsyncFinalInterceptor<TCommand, TResult>, IFinalInterceptor where TCommand : ICommand<in TResult>

typeParameters.name: TCommand
typeParameters.description: The type of command this interceptor handles. Must implement ICommand<TResult>.

typeParameters.name: TResult
typeParameters.description: The type of the result produced by the command.

types.name: ICommandFinalInterceptor<TCommand>
types.summary: Represents a final interceptor for commands in the pipeline.
types.remarks: A final interceptor is always executed at the end of the pipeline, after pre-, post-, and exception interceptors. It can observe the message, result, or exception, but should not modify the result directly. Use this interface to perform logging, cleanup, or any last-step operations in the command pipeline.
types.syntax: public interface ICommandFinalInterceptor<in TCommand> : ICommand, IMessage, IAsyncFinalInterceptor<TCommand>, IFinalInterceptor where TCommand : ICommand

typeParameters.name: TCommand
typeParameters.description: The type of command this interceptor handles. Must implement ICommand.

types.name: ICommandHandler<TCommand, TResult>
types.summary: Represents a handler for commands that produce a strongly-typed result.
types.remarks: Use this interface when you want type-safe handling of commands with a specific result type. The handler processes the command asynchronously and returns the strongly-typed result.
types.syntax: public interface ICommandHandler<in TCommand, TResult> : ICommand, IMessage, IAsyncHandler<TCommand, TResult>, IHandler where TCommand : ICommand<TResult>

typeParameters.name: TCommand
typeParameters.description: The type of command this handler processes. Must implement ICommand<TResult>.

typeParameters.name: TResult
typeParameters.description: The type of result produced by the command.

types.name: ICommandHandler<TCommand>
types.summary: Represents a handler for commands implementing ICommand.
types.remarks: This interface is non-generic regarding the result type; the command may or may not produce a result. For commands with a strongly typed result, consider using ICommandHandler<TCommand, TResult>.
types.syntax: public interface ICommandHandler<in TCommand> : ICommand, IMessage, IAsyncHandler<TCommand>, IHandler where TCommand : ICommand

typeParameters.name: TCommand
typeParameters.description: The type of command this handler processes. Must implement ICommand.

types.name: ICommandMediator
types.summary: Represents the mediator interface for sending commands within the application.
types.remarks: The command mediator is responsible for routing commands to their appropriate handlers and orchestrating the command handling pipeline. It ensures that commands are processed by exactly one handler and provides methods for sending commands both with and without expected results. In the CQRS pattern, commands represent intentions to change the system state. The command mediator helps maintain separation between the command issuers and the command handlers.
types.syntax: public interface ICommandMediator

types.name: ICommandPostInterceptor
types.summary: Represents a post-processing interceptor for commands that executes after any ICommand is handled.
types.remarks: This interceptor is non-generic and non-type-safe. It can be registered to run for multiple command types without specifying a particular result type. The HandleAsync method returns object, so any result modifications are handled via object references and casting. For scenarios where type safety is required, use the generic version: ICommandPostInterceptor<TCommand, TResult>.
types.syntax: public interface ICommandPostInterceptor : ICommand, IMessage, IAsyncPostInterceptor<ICommand>, IPostInterceptor

types.name: ICommandPostInterceptor<TCommand, TResult>
types.summary: Represents a type-safe post-interceptor for commands with a strongly-typed result. Executes after the command handler has completed and can modify the result before it propagates further through the pipeline.
types.remarks: TCommand is contravariant, matching the core IAsyncPostInterceptor<TMessage, TResult> contract the typed dispatch matches against. TResult must stay invariant: the typed member returns it.
types.syntax: public interface ICommandPostInterceptor<in TCommand, TResult> : ICommand, IMessage, IAsyncPostInterceptor<TCommand, TResult>, IPostInterceptor where TCommand : ICommand<TResult> where TResult : notnull

typeParameters.name: TCommand
typeParameters.description: The command type being intercepted. Must implement ICommand<TResult>.

typeParameters.name: TResult
typeParameters.description: The result type of the command. Also the type returned by the interceptor — for a narrower return type there is no third parameter anymore; return the base result type.

types.name: ICommandPostInterceptor<TCommand>
types.summary: Represents a post-processing interceptor for commands. This non-generic, non-type-safe version returns object from the pipeline.
types.remarks: Use this interface to register post-interceptors in the command pipeline without specifying a strongly-typed result. For type-safe scenarios, prefer using the generic version: ICommandPostInterceptor<TCommand, TResult>.
types.syntax: public interface ICommandPostInterceptor<in TCommand> : ICommand, IMessage, IAsyncPostInterceptor<TCommand>, IPostInterceptor where TCommand : ICommand

typeParameters.name: TCommand
typeParameters.description: The type of command this interceptor handles. Must implement ICommand.

types.name: ICommandPreInterceptor
types.summary: Represents a pre-interceptor for commands that is invoked before the command enters the pipeline. Can be used to modify the command or perform preparatory actions.
types.remarks: This is a non-generic, non-type-safe version of a pre-interceptor. It works with any command implementing ICommand. For type-safe interception, consider using ICommandPreInterceptor<TCommand> or ICommandPreInterceptor<TCommand, TModifiedCommand>.
types.syntax: public interface ICommandPreInterceptor : ICommand, IMessage, IAsyncPreInterceptor<ICommand>, IPreInterceptor

types.name: ICommandPreInterceptor<TCommand, TModifiedCommand>
types.summary: Represents a type-safe pre-interceptor for commands, allowing modification of the command before it enters the pipeline.
types.remarks: This interface is the type-safe variant of ICommandPreInterceptor. Use this when you want to ensure compile-time type safety while allowing the command to be modified before entering the pipeline. The HandleAsync method is called before the command is processed. The returned TModifiedCommand will continue through the pipeline as the new command.
types.syntax: public interface ICommandPreInterceptor<in TCommand, TModifiedCommand> : ICommand, IMessage, IAsyncPreInterceptor<TCommand>, IPreInterceptor where TCommand : ICommand where TModifiedCommand : TCommand

typeParameters.name: TCommand
typeParameters.description: The type of command being intercepted. Must implement ICommand.

typeParameters.name: TModifiedCommand

types.name: IQuery<TResult>

types.remarks: This interface extends IQuery and is intended for queries that return a specific result type when handled by a query handler. Implementing IQuery<TResult> allows the query to be registered within the query module and processed by type-safe query handlers and interceptors.

Implementations will receive queries as IQuery and results as object. For scenarios requiring type-safe handling of a specific query type and result type, consider using IQueryExceptionInterceptor<TQuery, TResult> instead.

types.name: IQueryFinalInterceptor
types.summary: Represents a non-generic final interceptor for queries, allowing custom logic to execute after all query handlers and other interceptors have completed.
types.remarks: This interface applies to all queries implementing IQuery. It inherits from the result-agnostic IAsyncFinalInterceptor<TMessage>, enabling asynchronous final processing of queries after they are dispatched to their handlers. The result-agnostic base is deliberate: a result-typed base (the previous IAsyncFinalInterceptor<IQuery, object>) is invisible to the pipeline's pattern match whenever the query result is a value type, so the final stage failed with NotSupportedException for such queries the moment it ran. The event module also supports simple POCO objects (plain old CLR objects), allowing them to be registered and used as events. types.name: IEventMediator

types.name: GeneratedDispatchRoots
types.summary: Process-wide store of generically instantiated dispatch roots, populated by source-generated registration code. Each root closes a dispatch generic over a concrete message (and result) type at compile time, letting the dispatch caches construct their pipeline executors and invokers without [MakeGenericType(params Type[])](https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/api/system.type.makegenerictype) — and giving Native AOT and trimming a static anchor for every instantiation, value-type messages and results included, which shared generic code cannot cover. The reflective MakeGenericType paths remain as the fallback for types without a root (open generics, runtime-only registrations).

members.summary: Roots a staged pipeline plan for a void message whose pipeline carries interceptor stages: bespoke straight-line code for the whole pipeline, replacing the runtime strategy's generic machinery. Advisory exactly like the single-handler plans — the hosting executor re-validates the plan's StagedPlanComposition against the registry per version and falls back to the runtime strategy on any mismatch. Idempotent.

members.name: AddVoidPlan<TMessage, THandler>()
members.syntax: public static void AddVoidPlan<TMessage, THandler>() where TMessage : IMessage where THandler : class, IAsyncHandler<TMessage>
members.summary: Roots a compile-time pipeline plan for a void message whose entire pipeline is a single async handler: the dispatch executor closes over both the message and the handler type, so the handler is invoked devirtualized — no contract pattern match. The plan is advisory: the executor re-validates the actual pipeline against the registry on every version change and falls back to the runtime dispatch shape whenever the pipeline no longer matches (interceptors registered at runtime, a different handler resolved, adapters configured). Idempotent.

members.name: AddVoidPlan<TMessage, THandler>(Func<IServiceProvider, THandler>)
members.syntax: public static void AddVoidPlan<TMessage, THandler>(Func<IServiceProvider, THandler> directHandlerFactory) where TMessage : IMessage where THandler : class, IAsyncHandler<TMessage>
members.summary: Variant of GeneratedDispatchRoots.AddVoidPlan<TMessage, THandler>() carrying a compile-time construction path for handlers with constructor dependencies: the generator emits static provider => new THandler(provider.GetRequiredService<TDep>(), ...) for handlers whose single public constructor takes only plain (or [FromKeyedServices]) service parameters — the one shape where the container's own constructor selection and the emitted construction provably coincide. The same advisory contract applies: the executor uses the factory only after verifying the handler's DI registration is the module's own plain transient one, and the dependencies resolve from the dispatching scope's provider exactly as container activation would resolve them. Idempotent.

members.name: AddVoidPlan<TMessage, THandler>(Func<THandler>)
members.syntax: public static void AddVoidPlan<TMessage, THandler>(Func<THandler> directHandlerFactory) where TMessage : IMessage where THandler : class, IAsyncHandler<TMessage>
members.summary: Variant of GeneratedDispatchRoots.AddVoidPlan<TMessage, THandler>() carrying a compile-time construction path for the handler: the generator emits static () => new THandler() for handlers with an accessible parameterless constructor that are not disposable. The factory is advisory like the plan itself — the executor uses it only after verifying at runtime that the handler's DI registration is the module's own plain transient one (no user factory, no lifetime override, not memoized), where container resolution and direct construction are semantically identical. Idempotent.

types.remarks: The plan is advisory: the hosting executor re-validates StagedVoidPlan.Composition against the live registry on every version change and falls back to the runtime strategy whenever the pipeline no longer matches, so a stale plan only loses its speedup, never changes behavior. types.name: AsyncBroadcastMediationStrategy<TMessage>
types.summary: Represents a mediation strategy that broadcasts a message asynchronously to all registered handlers of the specified TMessage.
types.remarks: This strategy ensures that: - All handlers for the message — including those registered for its base types and interfaces — are invoked sequentially, direct registrations first. - Pre-, post-, exception-, and final-interceptors are executed in the correct order. - Exceptions are captured and passed to the configured exception interceptors. Since this strategy is intended for event broadcasting, results are not adapted (unlike request/response message patterns).
